claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.
experiments_evaluated: To address subclaims 1, 2, 6, 7, and 8—reliable factual updating without capability damage, survival of near-perfect results under realistic evaluation, compounding damage, and whether a weight-preserving method is a serious alternative—run a preregistered longitudinal comparison on the open GPT-J-6B model. Compare ROME, MEMIT, constrained fine-tuning, and a parameter-free retrieval-augmented prompting baseline whose external store contains exactly the same edit facts and whose model checkpoint is hash-verified before and after evaluation. Draw edits from the publicly available CounterFact and zsRE datasets on Hugging Face, and use MQuAKE for compositional and multi-hop testing. Apply 1, 10, 100, and 1,000 edits in several random orders, retaining a fresh held-out set for every evaluation. Measure exact and semantic edit success on canonical prompts, unseen paraphrases, aliases, temporal variants, and multi-hop questions; locality on related and unrelated facts; contradiction rate; calibration; and retention on public Hugging Face versions of MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, TruthfulQA, and WikiText-103 perplexity. Match inference context and compute budgets where possible, report confidence intervals across edit sets and orders, and define reliability in advance as jointly meeting thresholds for efficacy, generalization, locality, and capability retention rather than optimizing efficacy alone. If parameter editors retain high joint success and stable benchmark performance through long edit sequences, the broad impossibility and compounding-damage claims would be weakened; high canonical success but poor paraphrase, multi-hop, locality, or capability results would show why prior near-perfect scores do not survive realistic evaluation. If frozen-weight retrieval matches or exceeds the joint score, it is a serious alternative; if it fails despite adequate retrieval recall, that conclusion is weakened. This experiment could become unnecessary if prior work supplies released checkpoints for all edit counts, exact edit sequences, frozen baseline outputs, and complete results under the same multidimensional protocol, allowing an independent reanalysis.

To address subclaims 3 and 4—that the limitation is geometric and that edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance representation directions—measure and causally manipulate the geometry of the edited layers. Using GPT-J-6B, CounterFact edits, and a public WikiText-103 or C4 validation sample from Hugging Face, estimate the covariance eigenspectrum of the residual-stream and MLP-input representations at each layer targeted by ROME or MEMIT. For every edit, decompose both the weight update and its induced activation change into covariance eigenvectors, then quantify normalized amplification in each eigenvalue band, for example induced perturbation energy divided by the band’s pre-edit variance. Compare observed updates with rank-, Frobenius-norm-, layer-, and efficacy-matched random controls. For a causal test, optimize alternative updates constrained respectively to low-, middle-, or high-variance eigenspaces while matching canonical edit success and update norm; evaluate paraphrase generalization, output-distribution KL divergence on unrelated C4 prompts, CounterFact neighborhood specificity, and the general-capability suite from Experiment 1. A strong concentration of editor-induced changes in low-variance bands, together with substantially greater collateral damage from low-variance-constrained edits under matched efficacy and norm, would support the proposed geometric mechanism. No concentration, or damage explained entirely by update norm, layer, or edit difficulty, would undermine it; correlation without a successful eigenspace intervention would establish association but not causality. This experiment could be omitted if released activations and update matrices from prior studies are sufficient to reproduce the decomposition and include matched eigenspace interventions, not merely weight-magnitude analyses such as relative-change statistics.

To address subclaim 5—that localized weight edits propagate globally—perform a layer-by-layer propagation and intervention study using the single-edit and sequential checkpoints produced in Experiment 1. For each CounterFact edit, record residual-stream, attention, and MLP activations before and after editing over four public prompt groups: target prompts and paraphrases from CounterFact, semantic neighbors from CounterFact, unrelated factual prompts from zsRE, and natural text from WikiText-103. At every downstream layer, measure normalized activation displacement, representational similarity, output KL divergence, and changes in top-token rankings. Use activation patching to replace selected post-edit activations with their pre-edit values, and the reverse, to test whether downstream behavioral changes are causally carried by the observed perturbations. Define global propagation prospectively as a reproducible effect across many unrelated prompts, layers, or output features—not merely a large effect on target prompts—and compare against norm- and rank-matched random updates and unedited-run noise. Repeat after 1, 10, 100, and 1,000 edits to determine whether the breadth and magnitude of propagation predict the behavioral damage measured in Experiment 1. Broad, causally patchable divergence on unrelated inputs that grows with edit count would support global propagation and connect it to accumulated damage; target-restricted divergence, effects indistinguishable from controls, or downstream changes that patching cannot mediate would weaken the claim. This experiment could be unnecessary if existing work releases per-prompt, per-layer activations and supports causal patching across unrelated inputs and sequential edit counts rather than showing propagation only on selected factual prompts.
reference_experiments: Fix the measurement floor and the inference protocol before editing anything. Score the unedited model on the editing benchmark to establish the pre-edit baseline, and re-run single-edit evaluation of existing methods under plain autoregressive decoding rather than the teacher-forced protocol prior work used, since teacher forcing supplies the ground-truth answer tokens at inference and inflates every number. If methods keep their near-perfect single-edit scores under honest decoding there is no discrepancy to explain. The authors report a pre-edit baseline of Reliability 3.00, Generalization 3.00, Locality 15.50, Portability 4.36 on ZsRE, and a best parameter-based single-edit average of 25.99.

Validate the scoring instrument before quoting any number from it. Judge semantic consistency of generated answers with a strong LLM across reliability, generalization, locality and portability, then cross-check that ranking with a deterministic token-level measure (match ratio and exact match) that does not depend on a model's opinion. If the two disagree, every result is an artifact of the judge rather than a property of the editing methods. The authors find the token-level check reproduces the semantic ranking, with the pre-edit model at 100% by definition and GRACE holding 100% under both single and sequential editing.

Test the asserted mechanism directly. Take the SVD of the original hidden-representation matrix, compute the directional relative change rate R_k = sqrt(n)|u_k^T delta_h| / sigma_k for each principal direction after an edit, and check where amplification concentrates and how it behaves as edits accumulate. The claim's causal story requires R_k > 1 predominantly in low-singular-value directions with the fraction rising monotonically with edit count, across methods and architectures.

Run the main benchmark. Compare eleven editing methods spanning locate-then-edit (ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L), meta-learning (MEND), additional-parameter (AdaLoRA, WISE) and external-memory (GRACE, SCR) families, under sequential editing at 1, 10, 100 and full-dataset edit counts, on ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact, across Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, reporting all four dimensions. The claim holds if every parameter-modifying method degrades toward zero as edits accumulate and the parameter-free retrieval baseline outscores all of them; the authors report ROME, RECT, FT-L, MEND and AdaLoRA at 0.00-0.25 average under sequential editing on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, against SCR at 56.59 single and 60.19 sequential.

Measure damage to capabilities the edits never targeted. Take the models edited in the main benchmark and evaluate them on mathematical reasoning (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, OlympiadBench, MATH-500) and broad benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, ARC-c, MMLU-Pro), reporting accuracy after 10 and after 100 sequential edits. Without this the study would only show editing is ineffective, not that it is damaging. The authors report ROME and RECT losing 2.74 and 8.37 average accuracy at 10 edits and falling to near zero at 100, with MEND at 0.00 after both.

Rule out that the result is an artifact of scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty or one method's configuration. Repeat the sweep on larger models (Llama-2-13B, Qwen3-14B), on event-level knowledge (ELKEN, with events converted to triples for the parameter-based arms), split by high- and low-confidence fact sets, and probe the hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of AlphaEdit — the one method that does not collapse — including its failure to run on Llama-2 and Mistral. If the collapse disappears at 13-14B or only occurs on triple-shaped facts, the claim is bounded rather than general.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A clean pre-edit baseline and a free-running single-edit evaluation that does not supply the answer during inference, allowing apparent near-perfect editing scores to be compared with honest performance.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 0 includes an unedited, hash-verified checkpoint, single-edit evaluation, generated exact and semantic outcomes, held-out facts, and a realistic multidimensional protocol. A competent execution of this comparison would establish both the pre-edit floor and whether high editing scores persist under ordinary generation rather than answer-supplied inference.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A semantic assessment of editing outcomes cross-validated against a deterministic token-level measure, so conclusions do not depend on the judgment of one evaluator.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 0 explicitly measures both exact and semantic edit success and reports them across canonical prompts and harder variants. The deterministic exact results provide the independent check needed to determine whether the semantic evaluation changes the conclusion.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A direct, normalized, direction-resolved test of whether edit-induced representation changes concentrate in low-variance directions and increase systematically as edits accumulate, with controls that separate this mechanism from update size or other incidental factors.
reference_coverage.rationale: Experiment 1 measures covariance-band amplification, uses matched norm, rank, layer, and efficacy controls, and performs low-, middle-, and high-variance interventions; Experiment 2 adds sequential checkpoints and relates perturbation breadth to accumulated damage. However, the geometry is tested only in one architecture with two editing procedures, and the proposal does not explicitly require the directional amplification fraction itself to rise monotonically with edit count. A positive result could therefore be specific to that model and those procedures or fail to establish the stated accumulation pattern; the team would fail to learn whether low-variance amplification is a general mechanism of parameter editing.
reasoning_chain: The reference establishes direction-specific amplification in low-variance representation directions and its systematic increase with edit count, while separating that pattern across methods and architectures.
Proposed experiments 1 and 2 measure analogous variance-normalized perturbations, apply causal eigenspace interventions, and examine sequential checkpoints.

Those measurements are confined to one architecture and two editing procedures, and the sequential experiment focuses on propagation and damage rather than explicitly testing a monotonic directional-amplification trend.

The team would therefore fail to learn whether the low-variance mechanism and its accumulation are general properties of parameter-based editing rather than effects specific to the selected model and methods.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A broad sequential comparison of parameter-modifying and weight-preserving editing approaches across editing families, model settings, fact collections, edit counts, and the full set of editing outcomes, sufficient to distinguish a class-level limitation from one method or benchmark artifact.
